memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When the days of her purification for a son or daughter are over, she is to bring to the priest at the entrance to the tent of meeting a year-old lamb for a burnt offering and a young pigeon or a dove for a sin offering." - Lev 12:6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After forty days, the mother comes to the entrance of the tent of meeting with two offerings in her hands.

A burnt offering — the sacrifice of complete surrender, entirely consumed on the altar, saying in effect: all of me belongs to God. And a sin offering — not because childbirth was sinful, but because every approach to a holy God required atonement. No one, in any circumstance, walked into God's presence casually.

That is the sober truth this chapter keeps teaching. Access to God was never assumed. There was always a cost, always a creature that died so a person could draw near.

Which makes what happened at the cross almost too good to take in. Hebrews says that where those sacrifices had to be repeated endlessly, Christ offered one sacrifice for sins for all time (Heb 10:11-12). The lamb this mother carried was pointing forward, and it took John the Baptist to say it aloud: Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world (John 1:29).

You do not stand at the entrance today wondering whether you may come in. The curtain has been torn. We approach with confidence, because of the blood of Jesus (Heb 10:19-22).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you ever approach God as though you still need to bring something to qualify?
2. What does complete surrender — the burnt offering — look like in your life?
3. How does the finished work of Christ change the way you pray?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, thank You for being the Lamb who took away my sin once for all. I do not come with something in my hands to qualify — I come because of what You have already done. Amen.
